title: The French and Indian War
objective: After this level you can explain how the war of 1754 to 1763 made Britain master of eastern North America but left it deep in debt.
summary: From 1754 to 1763 Britain and France, each with Native allies, fought for North America. Britain won Canada and the East, but its debt nearly doubled.

cards.headline: A skirmish in the Ohio woods grew into a war between empires.
cards.body: Britain won almost everything it fought for. Then it got the bill.

cards.headline: A young Virginian’s bad start
cards.body: In 1754 George Washington led Virginia troops to drive the French from the Ohio Valley. Outnumbered, he surrendered at Fort Necessity. It was the opening of the French and Indian War (1754 to 1763), the North American part of a wider war between Britain and France, the Seven Years’ War.

cards.headline: Choosing sides
cards.body: Native nations were not bystanders. France fought with many Native allies, such as the Shawnee, while Britain’s main Native partner was the Iroquois Confederacy.

mascot.line: It connects: the Iroquois Confederacy is Level 6’s Haudenosaunee, the league joined by the Great Law of Peace.

cards.headline: A plan for union
cards.body: At Albany in 1754, Benjamin Franklin proposed uniting the colonies under one council. The colonial assemblies and the Crown rejected it. The colonies would not yet act as one.

cards.headline: Winning big, owing big
cards.body: In the 1763 Treaty of Paris, Britain gained Canada and France’s lands east of the Mississippi except New Orleans, and Florida from Spain. But the war nearly doubled Britain’s national debt, and Britain expected the colonies to help pay it off. In 1763, Native nations of the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley attacked British forts in Pontiac’s War, and Britain then barred colonists from settling farther west.

cards.headline: The French and Indian War: explained
learned: The war (1754 to 1763) was part of the Seven Years’ War
Native nations fought on both sides
Franklin’s Albany Plan for union was rejected
Britain won big in 1763 but nearly doubled its debt

questions.prompt: What did Britain gain from France in the 1763 Treaty of Paris?

options.label: Louisiana and New Orleans
options.rationale: Britain gained the lands east of the Mississippi, but not New Orleans.

options.label: Canada and French lands east of the Mississippi
The Caribbean sugar islands only
options.rationale: The big prize was on the mainland.

options.label: Nothing; the war ended in a draw

questions.explanation: France gave Britain Canada and its lands east of the Mississippi, except New Orleans.

questions.prompt: Why did victory in 1763 leave Britain with a problem in its colonies?

options.label: Its debt nearly doubled, and it wanted colonists to help pay
The colonies refused to trade with Britain
options.rationale: The problem was the war’s cost.

questions.explanation: The war nearly doubled Britain’s national debt, and Britain expected the colonies to help pay it off.

questions.prompt: In Level 6, Franklin said that if the Six Nations could unite, the colonies should too. What did he propose at Albany in 1754?

options.label: A union of the colonies under one council
Moving the capital to Philadelphia
options.rationale: He proposed a council of the colonies.

questions.explanation: Franklin proposed uniting the colonies under one council; it was rejected.
